title: Native-round-recovery integration tests refuse a DATABASE_URL host query override
requirementRefs: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md Goal: 'what passes CI is what actually runs'; the build and release line is trustworthy

_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md Requirements: 'Real dependencies' (database and integration tests run on disposable environments) and 'Green honestly' (no test skipped or weakened)
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md Epic 1 NFR TEST-21 (test quality, PRD section 21); this story is Story 1.8, continuing Story 1.7, recorded only in its story spec (epics.md is not edited)
PRD/product-requirements.md section 21: database and integration tests run on disposable environments; PostgreSQL integration and concurrency tests
PRD/product-requirements.md section 15 row I: concurrency safety proven with tests on real PostgreSQL
PRD/product-requirements.md section 16 (security standard): least privilege and fail closed; a destructive test suite must not reach a database it was not pointed at
PRD/product-requirements.md section 24 gate 3: tests passing, with explicit evidence

Orchestrator investigation 2026-10-04 (TEST-PROVEN locally, no remote connection): Prisma 5.22 prisma-client-js (Rust query engine, no driver adapter) honours a host query parameter in DATABASE_URL in preference to the URL authority; with ?host=db.invalid and a matching opt-in, all 16 destructive recovery tests executed against the alternate target through integration-setup.ts, the Story 1.7 guard and PrismaService
architectureConstraints: Test-only scope: the implementation surface is apps/api/test/native-round-recovery.integration-spec.ts, limited to its safety guard and the directly relevant header comment; everything from describeOrSkip('native round recovery, against real PostgreSQL' to the end of the file is unchanged (native-round-recovery-suite-unchanged hashes it against the accepted Story 1.7 candidate)

Production code, Prisma configuration, schema and migrations (apps/api/prisma stays the migration authority, unchanged), PrismaService and withUtcSession, auth, API contracts, Go Core and staff/customer workflows do not change

apps/api/test/integration-setup.ts is unchanged: its INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL precedence, production-name refusal on the path database name and withUtcSession rewrite stay as they are. It enforces no host locality, and dbname/database query parameters did not override the database in this stack; that is recorded and no change is authorized there

CI is forbidden: .github/** does not change. Follow-up finding recorded, not in scope: CI DRIFT COULD FALSE-GREEN (api-integration stays green if the guard falls back to skipping); a separate CI-hardening story is required
The evaluator (tooling/**) and Story 1.7 evidence are immutable: Story 1.7's objective, anchor, spec, candidate, ledger and evidence are historical evidence, and its spec file is a forbidden surface

Fail-closed decision (orchestrator, binding): DATABASE_URL must not contain a host query parameter at all, whatever its value; the DECODED parameter name is compared case-insensitively, a strict superset of the engine's exact-name behaviour that also fails closed against a future case-insensitive driver. The guard does not reproduce the engine's effective-host algorithm

Evidence for the decision (orchestrator, 2026-10-04, measured in this runtime): authority db.invalid + ?host=127.0.0.1 connected to 127.0.0.1; authority localhost + ?host=db.invalid targeted db.invalid; the engine honours only the exact decoded name host (HOST/Host ignored; %68ost decoded and honoured); with repeated host the engine uses the LAST value while URLSearchParams.get returns the first; an empty host= still overrides; hostaddr, dbname and database are not honoured (the database always comes from the path); integration-setup.ts re-serializes the query through withUtcSession, so %68ost= reaches the guard as host=

Baseline rationale: the baseline is the accepted Story 1.7 candidate 0b89494821fe6a1def9dd1af0d2d30071325b957. The 16 recovery tests already run and pass there in the safe configuration, so RT-01 to RT-16 are regression characterizations, not baseline failures. The vulnerability is proven mechanically by native-round-recovery-fail-safe failing on the baseline: its six Story 1.7 cases pass, but every host-query case executes all 16 recovery tests and ?host=db.invalid attempts the alternate target
